instruction:
Convert this MySQL query to SQL Server:

SELECT * FROM orders ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 10;
output: SELECT TOP 10 * FROM orders ORDER BY created_at DESC;

SELECT user_id, STRING_AGG(item, ', ' ORDER BY item) AS items
FROM cart_items GROUP BY user_id;

INSERT INTO accounts (name) VALUES ('ada');
SELECT LAST_INSERT_ID() AS id;

SELECT NOW() AS now_utc, CURRENT_DATE - started::date AS age_days
FROM jobs;

SELECT id, to_char(created, 'YYYY-MM-DD') AS day
FROM events;

instruction:
Convert this PostgreSQL case-insensitive match to MySQL:

SELECT * FROM users WHERE email ILIKE '%@example.com';
output: SELECT * FROM users WHERE LOWER(email) LIKE '%@example.com';

instruction:
Convert this MySQL null handling to SQL Server:

SELECT IFNULL(nickname, username) AS display FROM users;
output: SELECT ISNULL(nickname, username) AS display FROM users;
SELECT * FROM products ORDER BY price LIMIT 5;

INSERT INTO settings (`key`, value) VALUES ('theme', 'dark')
ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE value = VALUES(value);

instruction:
Convert this SQL Server null handling to PostgreSQL:

SELECT ISNULL(price, 0) AS price FROM products;
output: SELECT COALESCE(price, 0) AS price FROM products;

SELECT DATEPART(year, ordered_at) AS yr, COUNT(*) AS n
FROM orders GROUP BY DATEPART(year, ordered_at);

instruction:
Convert this SQLite concatenation to MySQL:

SELECT first || ' ' || last AS full_name FROM customers;
output: SELECT CONCAT(first, ' ', last) AS full_name FROM customers;

instruction:
Convert this MySQL identifier quoting to PostgreSQL standard quoting:

SELECT `order`.`total`, `order`.`qty` FROM `order`;
output: SELECT "order"."total", "order"."qty" FROM "order";

instruction:
Convert this PostgreSQL cast syntax to standard ANSI SQL:

SELECT id::text, qty::int * 2 FROM inventory;
output: SELECT CAST(id AS TEXT), CAST(qty AS INTEGER) * 2 FROM inventory;

instruction:
Convert this SQLite boolean query to PostgreSQL:

SELECT * FROM flags WHERE active = 1 AND archived = 0;
output: SELECT * FROM flags WHERE active = TRUE AND archived = FALSE;

SELECT COALESCE(region, 'GLOBAL') AS region, CURRENT_DATE AS today
FROM stores;

instruction:
Convert this SQL Server conditional expression to PostgreSQL:

SELECT IIF(score >= 50, 'pass', 'fail') AS result FROM exams;
output: SELECT CASE WHEN score >= 50 THEN 'pass' ELSE 'fail' END AS result FROM exams;
